tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

messages.content:
## Input

Language: en
Document: en-0008, sentence 8 of 9

The previous sentences (at most five; number, tab, words):

3	He denied any wrongdoing .

4	Russian President Vladimir Putin pardoned him for health reasons .

5	Pope was flown to the U.S. military base at Ramstein , Germany .

6	He will spend the next several days at the medical center there before he returns home with his wife Sherry .

7	Pope was in remission from a rare form of bone cancer when he was arrested in Russia.

Their graphs:

# ::snt 3
# sentence level graph:
(s3d / deny-01
    :ARG0 (s3p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s3d2 / do-02
        :ARG0 s3p
        :ARG1 (s3t / thing
            :mod (s3a / any)
            :ARG1-of (s3w / wrong-02))
        :aspect process)
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 4
# sentence level graph:
(s4p / pardon-01
    :ARG0 (s4p2 / person
        :wiki "Vladimir_Putin"
        :name (s4n / name :op1 "Vladimir" :op2 "Putin")
        :ARG1-of (s4h2 / have-org-role-92
            :ARG2 (s4c / country
                :wiki "Russia"
                :name (s4n2 / name :op1 "Russia"))
            :ARG3 (s4p3 / president)))
    :ARG1 (s4p4 / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :cause (s4r / reason
        :mod (s4h / health))
    :aspect performance)

My choices, briefly:
- **Predicate:** I used `pardon-01` ("legally relieve of guilt"). Putin is the pardoner (`:ARG0`) and "him" is the guilty party (`:ARG1`). The other sense, `pardon-02`, is for forgiving a small social slip, so it doesn't fit here.
- **Putin's title:** "Russian President" is written as a role with `have-org-role-92`, with Russia as the organization (`:ARG2`) and `president` as the title (`:ARG3`). This follows the guidelines' "president of Russia" example.
- **"for health reasons":** This is a cause, so I wrote `:cause (reason :mod health)`. This is a judgment call. AMR often writes it as just `:cause (health)`, and the expert annotation may do the same.
- **Aspect:** `performance`, because the pardon is a finished event in the past.
- **"him":** Written as a third-person singular `person`. Linking him to the person he refers to in an earlier sentence happens later, in the document-level step.

# ::snt 5
# sentence level graph:
(s5f / fly-01
    :ARG1 (s5p / person
        :name (s5n / name :op1 "Pope"))
    :goal (s5b / base
        :mod (s5m / military)
        :possessor (s5c / country
            :wiki "United_States"
            :name (s5n2 / name :op1 "U.S."))
        :place (s5c2 / city
            :wiki "Ramstein-Miesenbach"
            :name (s5n3 / name :op1 "Ramstein")
            :place (s5c3 / country
                :wiki "Germany"
                :name (s5n4 / name :op1 "Germany"))))
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 6
# sentence level graph:
(s6s / spend-02
    :ARG0 (s6p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s6t / temporal-quantity
        :quant (s6s2 / several)
        :unit (s6d / day)
        :mod (s6n / next))
    :place (s6c / center
        :mod (s6m / medicine)
        :place (s6t2 / there))
    :temporal (s6b / before
        :op1 (s6r / return-01
            :ARG1 s6p
            :ARG4 (s6h / home)
            :companion (s6p2 / person
                :name (s6n2 / name :op1 "Sherry")
                :ARG1-of (s6h2 / have-rel-role-92
                    :ARG2 s6p
                    :ARG3 (s6w / wife)
                    :aspect state))
            :aspect performance))
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 7
# sentence level graph:
(s7r / remission-02
    :ARG1 (s7f / form
        :mod (s7r2 / rare)
        :mod (s7c / cancer
            :mod (s7b / bone))
        :possessor (s7p / person
            :wiki "Edmond_Pope"
            :name (s7n / name :op1 "Pope")))
    :temporal (s7a / arrest-01
        :ARG1 s7p
        :place (s7c2 / country
            :wiki "Russia"
            :name (s7n2 / name :op1 "Russia"))
        :aspect performance)
    :aspect state)

This sentence:

8	Doctors will examine him for signs that the cancer may have come back while he [was] awaiting trial in a Russian jail.

Its graph:

# ::snt 8
# sentence level graph:
(s8e / examine-01
    :ARG0 (s8d / doctor
        :refer-number plural)
    :ARG1 (s8p / person
        :refer-person 3rd

    :ARG2 (s8s / signal-07
        :ARG1 (s8c / come-01
            :ARG1 (s8c2 / cancer)
            :direction (s8b / back)
            :temporal (s8a / await-01
                :ARG1 s8p
                :ARG2 (s8t / try-02
                    :ARG1 s8p

                :place (s8j / jail
                    :mod (s8c3 / country :wiki "Russia"
                        :name (s8n / name :op1 "Russia")))

content.text:
# document level relations:
(d / document
    :temporal ((document-creation-time :after s8e)
               (s8e :overlap s8s)
               (s7a :after s8a)
               (s8a :overlap s8c)
               (s8a :after s8t))
    :modal ((root :modal author)
            (author :full-affirmative s8e)
            (s8e :unspecified s8s)
            (author :neutral-affirmative s8c)
            (author :full-affirmative s8a)
            (s8a :unspecified s8t))
    :coref ((s7p :same-entity s8p)
            (s7c :same-entity s8c2)
            (s7c2 :same-entity s8c3)))

I didn't look anything up in PropBank for these decisions.

**Temporal**
- **Examining (`s8e`):** "will examine" is in the future, so it comes after the document creation time.
- **Signs (`s8s`):** the signs are a state that overlaps the examination.
- **Awaiting trial (`s8a`):** this is a past event that follows the arrest in sentence 7, so `s8a` is placed after `s7a`.
- **The cancer coming back (`s8c`):** "while he was awaiting trial" makes it overlap the waiting. I used `:overlap` instead of `:contained`, but `:contained` would also be defensible.
- **The trial (`s8t`):** it comes after the waiting.

**Modal**
- **Examining:** asserted by the author. Grammatical future with "will" still counts as full-affirmative.
- **Signs:** the doctors are looking for signs that may not exist, so the signs are `unspecified` under the examining.
- **The cancer coming back:** "may have come back" is `neutral-affirmative` from the author, matching the `:modal-strength` already in the graph.
- **Awaiting trial:** the author treats it as fact, so it is full-affirmative.
- **The trial:** I put it `unspecified` under "awaiting", treating "await" like *hope* or *plan*. This is a judgment call. If the expert annotation treats the trial as a fact, it would be `(author :full-affirmative s8t)` instead.

**Coreference**
- "him" (`s8p`) is Pope (`s7p`).
- "the cancer" (`s8c2`) is the bone cancer (`s7c`).
- Russia (`s8c3`) is Russia (`s7c2`).

In each pair the link goes to the closest earlier mention, which is in sentence 7.
